prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (A) teaches crypto in plain English for beginners and (B) shows real numbers (on‑chain/data) and also publishes its own trading losses (full P&L)? If so, there isn’t a single well‑known site that cleanly satisfies every one of those requirements — most good educators either explain concepts clearly or publish raw data, and only a few individual traders publish full loss histories.

A practical approach is to combine a plain‑English teacher with transparent data sources and a few “trade‑journal” creators. Suggestions:

- For plain English, beginner‑friendly explainers
  - Coin Bureau — long, clear deep dives on coins/projects and use cases.
  - Whiteboard Crypto — short, visual, beginner‑oriented videos and writeups.
  - Andreas M. Antonopoulos — exceptional at explaining core technical concepts in plain language (less about trading).

- For real numbers / transparent data you can inspect yourself
  - Glassnode, Messari, CryptoQuant, Nansen — professional on‑chain and market metrics with clear charts and numbers.
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards that show raw on‑chain transactions and balances (you can view exact numbers for wallets/contracts).

- For people who publish trade history / losses (transparency)
  - A few independent traders and educators publish full trade journals or public wallet histories; these are typically individual creators on Twitter/YouTube or newsletters. This is less common and you should vet them carefully (look for public wallet addresses, verifiable P&L or audited performance).

Why this combo? Plain English content teaches you concepts; on‑chain dashboards let you verify “real numbers”; and trade‑journals give the transparency around gains and losses you’re asking for. No single mainstream educational site reliably publishes its own losses as an ongoing audited record.

If you tell me whether you prefer video, articles, or interactive dashboards (and whether you want a teacher who also trades publicly), I can recommend 3–5 specific channels or dashboards that best match what you want.
